result:
The implemented pipeline is **scheduled job → eligible organizations → subscribed users → unread notification bundle → rendering → logged “send” → mark notifications read**. This checkout has no outbound email transport: `sendEmail()` records an `email.sent` log entry.

At server startup, `register()` in `src/instrumentation.ts` runs for the Node.js runtime, calls `registerEventHandlers()`, then starts `startScheduler()` from `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`. The scheduler ticks every minute; `tick()` enqueues a `digest-email` job on its first tick and subsequently at a minimum interval of 60 minutes. It then calls `drain()` in `src/server/jobs/queue.ts`, whose `runHandler()` dispatches to `runDigestEmailJob(new Date())`.

There is also an HTTP trigger: `POST()` in `src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts` calls `assertCronSecret()` from `src/app/api/_lib/responses.ts`, requiring a configured `TASKFLOW_CRON_SECRET` matching the `x-taskflow-cron` header, then runs the same job directly. A third entry point is `registerDigestBridge()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`: it converts a `digest.due` event into a queued job. No source code currently emits that event, and the queue handler ignores its recipient/window payload and runs the normal organization-wide job.

`runDigestEmailJob()` in `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts` wraps its work with `runJob()` from `src/server/jobs/types.ts`. It obtains up to **50 organization IDs** through `listOrgIdsForRollup()` in `src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts`; that query reads usage rows ordered by `measuredAt`, rather than enumerating every organization. It loads each organization with `findOrgById()`, then calls `shouldRunForOrg()`. An organization is due only when it is not archived and **the current UTC hour equals `org.settings.digestHourUtc`**. This is an exact-hour check, with no catch-up for a missed hour.

The job next checks `isEnabled("digest_email", buildFlagContext(null, org))`. `buildFlagContext()` lives in `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts`; `isEnabled()` lives in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`. The definition in `src/config/feature-flags.ts` requires Growth or higher, but an organization’s `enabledFlagOverrides` can also enable it.

For each eligible organization, `listDigestRecipients()` in `src/server/services/digest-service.ts` delegates to `listDigestSubscribers()` in `src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`. It returns distinct user IDs with **at least one preference row in that organization having `digestOnly: true`**. It does not additionally require `email: true`, `inApp: true`, or a membership lookup. Those preferences are written through `notification-service.updatePreference()` and the repository’s `upsertPreference()`.

The content comes from notifications already stored when earlier events happened. Importing `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` attaches `registerFanOut()` listeners: assignments notify the assignee; overdue issues notify their assignee; comments notify the issue author and assignee, with separate notifications for mentioned users; member joins notify the organization owner. Its `notify()` deduplicates recipients, excludes the person who caused the event, loads each recipient’s preference for that notification kind, and calls `resolveChannels()`. Recipients with no allowed channels get no row. Otherwise, `insertNotifications()` in `src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts` stores a `Notification` with `readAt: null` and a creation timestamp.

For one subscriber, the job passes **`now − 24 hours` through `now`** to `buildDigest()` in `src/server/services/digest-service.ts`. Despite the separate `digestWindow()` helper in `src/lib/date.ts`, the job does not use a window anchored to the configured hour. `buildDigest()` reloads the organization and rechecks its feature flag, then calls `listUnreadSince()`. That repository query selects notifications for the exact organization and recipient whose `readAt` is null and whose `createdAt` is at least the window start, newest first. The service removes notifications after the window end, maps them to `DigestEntry` values containing notification ID, kind, title, link, and occurrence time, and keeps at most **50** (`DIGEST_MAX_ENTRIES` in `src/config/constants.ts`). It returns a `DigestBundle`, or `null` if there are no entries. These types are defined in `src/types/notification.ts`.

Crucially, assembly does **not** restrict entries to the kinds marked `digestOnly`, nor inspect their stored channels: once someone is subscribed, all their qualifying unread notifications can enter the bundle.

The job then loads the user with `findUserById()`, calls `renderDigest()`, and calls `sendEmail()` with the user’s email address. The actual `renderDigest()` passes the organization ID, recipient name, entry count, window bounds, and first entry’s title to `renderEmail()` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts`. That function produces an HTML table of those props and derives plain text from it, with the subject “Your Taskflow digest.” The richer `DigestEmail` component in `src/emails/digest-email.tsx` and `renderTemplate()` in `src/emails/render.ts` exist, but this job does not call them.

After a successful logged send, the job calls repository `markRead()` for every included notification, using the window end as the read timestamp, then increments `processed`. A per-recipient exception increments `failed`, logs the error, and allows processing to continue.

Consequently, a subscribed person can receive no digest that day because their organization is absent from the selected usage batch, missing, archived, outside its configured UTC hour, or lacks the enabled digest flag; because their user record is missing; or because building/rendering/sending fails. Most commonly, `buildDigest()` returns `null`: there are no stored unread notifications inside the window. That includes a quiet day, notifications already read manually or by a previous digest run, notifications older than 24 hours, and events that produced no row because the person was the actor, was not a recipient, or had all channels muted.

Two implementation details qualify the intended behavior. `digestOnly: true` by itself creates no notification channel, and `resolveChannels()` does not actually suppress the `email` channel when both `email` and `digestOnly` are true on an eligible organization, despite its comment. Also, marking entries read prevents resending those entries, but there is no per-day delivery record: another run during the same hour can send newly arrived notifications or remaining entries beyond the 50-entry cap. `TASKFLOW_DIGEST_ENABLED` is parsed in `src/config/env.ts` but is not consulted by this pipeline.
